newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds Chemists sees bid climax approaching.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds Chemists sees bid climax approaching.

text.p: Pharmacy and retail group Lloyds Chemists Plc said on Wednesday it expects rival suitors UniChem Plc and Gehe AG to meet the British government's conditions, paving the way for fresh takeover bids.
In July the government said bids for Lloyds by either UniChem or Gehe could go ahead if certain assets were sold off.

"The board of Lloyds Chemists is not aware that any major difficulties have arisen in the fulfilment of the conditions laid down, and expects the terms of the necessary undertakings by UniChem and Gehe to be finalised by 18 October," chairman Allen Lloyd said in a statement.
In March rival bids from UniChem and Gehe lapsed when they were referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The government then said the bids could proceed if the bidders had agreements in principle to sell some of Lloyds' pharmaceutical wholesaling businesses.

Lloyds said in August it had received numerous offers from prospective purchasers for these operations. It said both UniChem and Gehe had said they wanted to comply with the conditions and Lloyds said the two firms were "currently in discussions with the competition authorities." --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
